cohorts.subjects: Six fresh-frozen cadaveric lumbar spines (L1-L5) from an accredited US tissue bank (Science Care, Phoenix, Arizona), studied at Rush University Medical Center, Chicago; all donors free from spine-related conditions or spine surgery; causes of death in Table 1 (COPD, heart attack, cardiac arrest in two, atherosclerotic heart disease, chronic heart failure); ethnicity not stated; no other inclusion or exclusion criteria given; IRB exempt as cadaveric tissue. Left and right pedicles of L1-L5 were cut out at the pedicle-body and pedicle-lamina junctions for micro-CT. Weight 40.8-127.5 kg, height 160.0-193.0 cm, BMI 15.4-42.2 (Table 1). How the levels were identified, and whether any spine was transitional, is not stated.
cohorts.n_units: 60 pedicles (left and right, L1-L5) of 6 lumbar spines; vertebral bodies L1-L5 for HU (n = 30)

Lumbar pedicles L1-L5 measured by CT, as quoted; the reference title names an Indian population (Mitra SR et al. 2002, Spine, ref. 11); number, ages and sexes not given here. Lumbar pedicles of women and men, L1-L5, measured on CT, as quoted; the reference title says reformatted CT images (Li B et al. 2004, Spine, ref. 8); number and ages not given here. Rows carry source_of_values Li et al. [8].
Tibia and radius cortical bone, as quoted (Burghardt AJ et al. 2010, J Bone Miner Res, ref. 24); subjects not described here. Rows carry source_of_values Burghardt et al. [24].

techniques.instrument: Scanco muCT 50 (55 kV, 145 uA, 34.4 um voxels, matrix 1024 x 1024), each pedicle in distilled water in a 35 mm tube; reslicing in Mimics (Materialise); lengths and areas in ImageJ
techniques.how: Pedicle axis = line through the centroids of cross-sections at the anterior and posterior thirds of the pedicle; cross-sections taken perpendicular to that axis; the isthmus is the section with the shortest minor (transverse) axis. On it: transverse diameter = length on the minor axis, longitudinal diameter = length on the major (longest) axis, outer surface to outer surface; medial and lateral wall thickness on the minor axis and cranial and caudal wall thickness on the major axis, from the medullary-cavity boundary (judged over a few slices around the isthmus) to the outer surface; areas of the whole section and of the medullary cavity (Table 2). Sides pooled or averaged is not stated for Table 2.
techniques.magnification: Not applicable: a calibrated micro-CT volume of the excised pedicle, 34.4 um voxels; no projection.
techniques.observers: Not stated (no observer count, no repeatability).

techniques.instrument: Same micro-CT scans; custom Visual C++ routine
techniques.how: On the isthmus section, binarised at threshold = (cortical bone grey level - background grey level) x 0.5; four 30 deg sector ROIs measured from the 12 o'clock direction set by the major axis (cranial +/-15 deg, medial 75-105, caudal 165-195, lateral 255-285), each spanning the wall between the cavity boundary and the outer surface (Fig 2B); bone area fraction = bone pixels / ROI pixels x 100. Left and right were averaged since they did not differ. Summarised by donor (Table 3) and by level (Table 4).
techniques.magnification: Not applicable: calibrated micro-CT volume, a ratio of pixel counts.

techniques.instrument: ImageJ; the CT scanner used is not stated (Inference: the clinical CT of Fig 4, Siemens Volume Zoom)
techniques.how: Largest possible elliptical ROI in each vertebral body on all axial CT slices of L1-L5, excluding osseous abnormalities and voids such as vascular channels, after Schreiber et al. [19]; used to judge osteoporosis (L1 below 110 HU, Pickhardt [20]) and correlated with the average pedicle-wall bone area fraction (n = 30). No HU values are printed.

techniques.instrument: Siemens Volume Zoom; 120 kV, 100 mA, field of view 272 mm, matrix 512 x 512, slice thickness 0.625 mm, increment 1.0 mm
techniques.how: A clinical CT image of the pedicle isthmus of one specimen shown beside its micro-CT image to show the loss of wall detail; no measurement from it is reported.

within_paper: One cohort only. Every value of this paper's own comes from the same six donors of Table 1 (p. 2, PDF 2): the isthmus dimensions (Table 2) and the bone area fraction (Tables 3 and 4, Results text) were both measured on the same micro-CT scans of the same 60 pedicles (p. 2-5, PDF 2-5); Table 3 (by donor) and Table 4 (by level) summarise the same side-averaged bone area fraction values two ways, and the Results' regional averages (p. 5) are a third summary of them; the vertebral body HU (p. 5) were measured on the L1-L5 bodies of the same spines, and Fig 4's clinical CT is of one of the same specimens (p. 10, PDF 10). The two donors with L1 below 110 HU (a 66-year-old man and a 50-year-old woman, p. 5) are among the six. Inference: by age and sex they are donors 6 and 2 of Table 1. The paper does not say whether the HU CT was taken before or after the pedicles were cut out.
